lines.text: Out here, the night has a glow to it.
Gas with nowhere to go… burning in the dark.
The answer was born nearly six thousand miles away — in Florence, at the Pignone foundry, in 1842.
lines.say: The answer was born nearly six thousand miles away. In Florence, at the [Pignone](/pinjˈoʊneɪ/) foundry, in eighteen forty-two.

lines.text: It became Nuovo Pignone. It mastered compressors, then gas turbines — first under license from GE, then as part of GE.
lines.say: It became [Nuovo Pignone](/nwˈɔːvoʊ pinjˈoʊneɪ/). It mastered compressors, then gas turbines. First under license from G E, then as part of G E.

lines.text: Today, it is Baker Hughes.
In 2013, its engineers began a new turbine, built on decades of proven design.
lines.say: In twenty thirteen, its engineers began a new turbine, built on decades of proven design.

lines.text: They called it NovaLT.
lines.say: They called it Nova L T.

lines.text: Air. Twelve stages, squeezed nineteen to one.
lines.say: Air... Twelve stages, squeezed nineteen to one.

lines.text: Fire. One ring of flame, fed by thirty-nine premixers, holding NOx under fifteen parts per million.
Its combustor has been tested on up to one hundred percent hydrogen.
Motion. Seven thousand eight hundred revolutions a minute.
Power. Sixteen point nine megawatts, and thirty-five thousand hours between maintenance.
The first went to work on a Canadian pipeline in 2017.
lines.say: The first went to work on a Canadian pipeline in twenty seventeen.

lines.text: Now they're ordered by the dozen — for data centers, and for the oilfield.
lines.say: Now they're ordered by the dozen. For data centers, and for the oilfield.

lines.text: Back in West Texas, the Permian produces nearly twenty-eight billion cubic feet of gas a day — more than its pipelines can carry.
lines.say: Back in West Texas, the Permian produces nearly twenty-eight billion cubic feet of gas a day. More than its pipelines can carry.

lines.text: This year, gas at Waha traded below zero for ninety days straight.
And yet, the field is short of power. Demand could reach twenty-six gigawatts by 2038 — and new lines are years away.
lines.say: And yet, the field is short of power. Demand could reach twenty-six gigawatts by twenty thirty-eight. And new lines are years away.

lines.text: Too much gas. Not enough power.
So what if the gas never had to leave?
The fuel the field can't sell, becoming the power it can't get — made right on site, behind the meter.
lines.say: The fuel the field can't sell, becoming the power it can't get. Made right on site, behind the meter.

lines.text: That's the opportunity for Baker Hughes: gas-to-power, as a service.
lines.say: That's the opportunity for Baker Hughes. Gas to power, as a service.

lines.text: NovaLT turbines, running on field gas at the pad — owned, operated, and watched around the clock by Baker Hughes.
lines.say: Nova L T turbines, running on field gas at the pad. Owned, operated, and watched around the clock, by Baker Hughes.

lines.text: The operator doesn't buy a power plant. They buy power, by the megawatt-hour.
lines.say: The operator doesn't buy a power plant. They buy power, by the [megawatt hour](/mˈɛɡəwˌɑːt ˈaʊɚ/).

lines.text: Seventeen megawatts at a time. Two can run an electric frac fleet.
Moved when the field moves. Added as it grows.
lines.say: Moved, when the field moves. Added, as it grows.

lines.text: The same fire that lit the night…
finally put to work.
